newsitem.title: USA: Russia ponders Mir space station repairs.
newsitem.headline: Russia ponders Mir space station repairs.

text.p: Russian space authorities were considering spacewalks to restore some power to the stricken Mir space station, but any repair would be difficult, NASA officials said on Thursday.

Spacewalks to tap the power of the module damaged in Wednesday's collision with an unmanned cargo craft could be attempted in July, said Frank Culbertson, who heads NASA's cooperation programme with Mir.
"I think it is going to be a very difficult job," he said. "I don't think you can take it lightly. It's going to be interesting for the world to watch this."
The space station lost half its power supply when the airtight hull of the Spektr science module was ruptured in the crash.

Under the plan being discussed, cosmonauts in space suits would run cables from the module's electricity-generating solar arrays to the space station's other compartments, Culbertson said. The rewiring operation could possibly be attempted from inside the depressurized module.
The repairs would restore power from three of Spektr's solar panels. A fourth panel, badly damaged in the orbital crash, was probably unusable.

The Mir crew, cosmonauts Vasily Tsibliev and Alexander Lazutkin, and NASA astronaut Michael Foale, were forced to shut down most of the station's systems, inlcuding some life support systems, to save power.
The crew were rearranging batteries to get the maximum charge possible from the remaining solar panels. The station's most efficient batteries were lost when Spektr was sealed off.
NASA officials thought the chances of repressurizing the punctured module were slim.
Culbertson said it was too soon to consider the future of NASA's missions to Mir.
Two more U.S. astronauts were to spend time on Mir and the station now relies on the shuttle to deliver 40 percent of its supplies and equipment.
"It would be more of a problem for the Russians to support the Mir without the shuttle coming and going," Culbertson said. "We would not be very good partners if we stopped going there."
A new Progress cargo craft, originally scheduled for launch on Friday, was being delayed so repair gear and replacements for equipment lost in the accident could be shipped to Mir.
Foale, who lost his sleeping quarters in the orbital collision, asked the ground to send up a new toothbrush, an electric shaver and a pair of running shoes.
Although the British-born astronaut lost many of his personal items and science gear in the Spektr module, he seemed cheerful in transmissions to the ground released by NASA.
"Mike sounds very positive and upbeat," Culbertson said. He sees it as a quite interesting adventure at this point."
